title: Resistance is a squeeze
description: Resistance squeezes the path. More ohms means less current. Zero ohms is not a super lamp — it is a short.

blocks.md:
## A narrow path versus a wide one

Resistance is how much the path squeezes the flow. A large resistance is a narrow door: less current for the same push. A small resistance is a wide door: more current. The lamp itself has resistance. A separate resistor is a knob you can see.

This bites when you treat ohms as a brightness slider that ignores voltage, or when you chase zero ohms for “maximum light.” Zero ohms is a short. Current tries to become huge. Heat follows.

![Resistance squeezes the path](assets/resistance-squeeze.svg)

```text
same V, large R  →  small I
same V, small R  →  large I
R = 0            →  short (danger)
```

A common mistake is “turn ohms to zero so it is brightest.” The questions ask you to keep resistance as a squeeze, not a cheat.

blocks.promptMd: If you raise resistance and keep the same battery, current…

choices.md: Falls — the path is a tighter squeeze
Rises, because resistance is a brightness knob
Should be set to zero for a better lamp

blocks.explainMd: Same push, tighter squeeze, smaller I. Zero ohms is a short, not a win.

blocks.promptMd: Same 1-cell battery. Guess the current when ohms is 2. (I ≈ 1 / ohms)
blocks.explainMd: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5. Nearby answers still show you have the squeeze idea.

blocks.promptMd: Setting resistance to zero is the safe way to get the brightest lamp.
blocks.explainMd: Zero ohms is a short. Current and heat soar. The cap fails.
